reviews.text: For new players assuming that this newer version of the game is better than the original, you would be wrong. Maybe it will be, someday, but not in its current state. It is buggy and broken. These are not the same developers that created the original, and they are struggling to make everything work properly. It is currently mid September and there hasn't been an update since early April. Maybe it will get fixed, maybe it won't. Many have been giving this game a positive rating based on what they hope it will become, and love for the original game, but I think that is unfair to players who see the positive rating and think that it is in a good, playable state. Notice the low number of hours played on many of the positive reviews. That tells you the actual state of the game. Too many early access games stay there for years, or never leave EA, for me to give a positive review based on what may, or may not, happen. Considering that this version costs 4x more than the original game, the original game is, currently, the better way to go. It's not perfect, but stuff works. If you do choose to buy the original game, make sure to get the Complete Edition mod for all of the extra ghosts, bug fixes, and polish. If the game ever gets to a good place, I will be more than happy to change this to a glowing review, but until then I can't recommend it. Update: Nov. 2025 we finally got an update to the game. It seems to add more content, but they still have not got all of the powers working correctly. It's frustrating that you know how they are supposed to work, from playing the original game, and they simply don't work in this remake. I'm not sure why they focused on adding new content before fixing the powers. I will update this review as things progress.

I thought that was weird because I didn't see an AI disclosure when I looked at the store page earlier in the day. So I check again and see the disclosure is there now AND I discovered that it was only added a few hours before. Incredibly gross behavior from the developers. *EDIT* Game was gifted to me when it came out, more detailed review to come but I would still rate it not recommended

I avoid giving negative reviews because I believe they have a disproportionate impact on Steam's algorithm. I feel less inclined to do so when I'm doing this for a remake of a childhood favourite. However I believe that having AI generated assets in a game, without using Steam's disclosure until someone else leaves a negative review pointing this out, is a very bad business practice that warrants being pointed out and this is my only way of doing so. This feels like an especially bad approach to the matter when the usage of AI generation is restricted to creating assets that stick out horribly due to not fitting the game's style, have no impact on gameplay, and would have looked more endearing if the developers had commissioned some low effort graphic designer to slap something together for a low rate. I'll use this opportunity, in case the omission of using AI assets does not bother you in the slightest, to provide some feedback exclusively pertaining to the game. I believe the addition of new clutter to locations helps them look "lived in", but they were placed without much thought, resulting in objects like a Television not having the "Electrical" Fetter which is quite silly. I think Unreal Engine's Lumen is a bad tool and the game looks fine without it. NPCs get regularly stuck in doorways and are only broken out of that state by other NPCs giving them a "push" to change the pathing. The skill tree is poorly implemented, flat stat bonuses are boring no-brainers that involve zero decision making. I will however note, that I did not experience the amount of bugs and crashes that a lot of people here mention after completing 3 out of 4 missions in Act 1, I assume updates fixed a good portion of those or they're just relevant in later content.

Just finished the game. I played through the original like 7 times before, so I knew what to do. With the new content which are [spoiler] a bunch of new ghosts in old levels, 4 new-ish levels (3 entirely new, military base once again for a new finale) and new ghosts in the new levels each with their own requirements of unlocking them. [/spoiler] All in all it took me about 9 hours to complete it. Took me a few restarts on some of the levels to unlock a few specific ghosts - looking at you, Fingers and Bridget - because the unlock conditions got scared and unreliable. Also a bunch of restarts because the recommended roster got switched up and I didn't pay attention. I basically took a wrong team into it. Levels are replayable for more Gold Plasma and Pumpkins - Oh yeah there are Pumpkins now! More on them in a moment - In the original, if I recall correctly, you would only top off on Gold Plasma when you got a new highscore on a previously visited location. Gold Plasma is needed to buy more powers for your team. Considering there is a hard cap, you could never buy ALL the powers for ALL your ghosts. You would often stick to a team and barely ever change it, unless you find a new ghost that fills a niche and is very versatile or just very powerfull on its own. This on its own also makes the game more replayable. You are awarded a bunch of Gold Plasma and 3 Pumpkins (You can probably get between 0-3 depending on your performance, but I have never gotten less than 3) after each level. There is a new skilltree to spec into in the hub level, most of those skills costing 6 Pumkings each, 3 super skills each to the left and to the right that cost more and all the way to the end the ultimate skill - another ghost slot. By the time I played throug each level once, I have skilled all the way to the left side, I am basically two thirds through. [h3] What I like [/h3] The price! At the point of writing, the winter sale it is currently a whopping 50% off! That is about 10 bucks and if you have nostalgia for this game, go right ahead! The music! Never gets old. I think they even added a few more tracks when you are about to chase off your last few mortals. You can respec your ghosts taught powers! In the old game you were stuck with your choice, this makes all your ghosts more versatile and you can experiment. The gameplay on is just so good and addicting! Nostalgia! The reason most people would pick this up. [h3] What I do not like [/h3] The take the recommended team button got tinkered with. Not sure if it is a good thing or a bad thing as it is a big plus in trying different combinations. Unlike in the original, where you would get a static team that is well suited for the task at hand as well as unlocking the new ghosts in the level, this one seemingly gets you a random team every time. I think I also recall it giving me a team that would absolutely not get me a ghost unlocked, if I recall correctly, so I had to change. I am not the biggest fan on the graphics. What I want to say is, I liked the old jagged looks better. It had it's own charme. It is also rather taxing on my system. It is outdated I admit, but the remake of a game from the 2000s should not bring my gpu from 8 years ago to 80% at all times. Also, what is the UI in the options? A slider for basically everything, EVEN the language settings is a bit questionable. The marketing. Seriously I did not know this game exists until 2 days ago when I bought it. I was randomly browsing through steam and found this by pure chance. I LOVE Ghost Master and had no idea this existed! To be fair, the original came out in 2003 and I had no clue there is work done on a remaster, so I wasn't looking for anything, but I bet there are a lot more people that love the original that have no clue this exists. In a world where sadly a lot of remasters end up as moneygrabs, this one shines through through passion and staying itself. Highly appreciated. At this point the game is a solid 8/10 for me.

I probably replay the original Ghost Master once every year or so. It’s clunky but nostalgic and extremely fun and there’s no other game that really scratches the itch. I missed this coming out, and had redownloaded and played through the first 1.5 Acts on the original, found this, and immediately replayed. Good: the game is (moderately) less clunky. Haven’t run into the same glitches as other people - there are a few things that don’t work exactly the same as the original (Quake is less overpowered to fix most environmental puzzles). Have not run into the same glitch issues that others have complained about (yet), but the game seems less buggy than the original (especially re: stairwell glitches). Missions are significantly faster: I took about 20 minutes to run Usual Suspects on the original, and then ran it in about half that on the new one. This really shows in missions like Phantom of the Operating Room that were excruciating in the original game. Mid: there’s a camera quirk where clicking “go to” centers the view directly above a ghost/mortal rather than the angle of view you had before. This wouldn’t be an issue if there was a snapback camera command or angle key, but there’s not.

Is it true?! The classic ghost game returned?! I can not tell you how much I LOVED this game. Owning a physical PC copy decades ago, and picking it up again when it became digital a remaster I thought was never going to happen because of how obscure the game is. I did not hesitate to grab it at full price. Now, there are two very big negatives this has going for it. The first: Unreal Engine 5. Games that use U.E.5 need to come with a disclaimer because the engine is AWFUL, even when it runs smooth and works your PC will CHUG, welcome to your new airport in your own home. Also pre-made assets, this I do not mind as some of them actually give a face lift to the original and help it. The second: Generative A.I. It's easy to spot but they have worked with the AI to make it have that old school feeling with a graphics update. If you are so against GenAI in games then avoid this entirely. But if you can look past this, this has been kept in its almost original condition. Besides these two issues, the game itself? It's nearly a perfect one-to-one recreation of the original, and even has the option to use the original soundtrack. The opening cutscene is the original cutscene only stretched out for widescreen. The voice lines are the same and the files are from the original as well. The only thing I have noticed that has been cut is the female voice over when visiting the Ghoul Room. Speaking of the Ghoul Room, you now have upgrades! Yes, that pumpkin score now offers you pumpkins to upgrade some effects. Such as giving a certain percentage more terror, or believe. A nice addition to help clear levels faster as some levels in the original could take far too long. They also have put in all new levels with a roadmap for even more! The season pass I grabbed as well because if there is one thing I always wanted, it was more Ghost Master! If you love the original you will love this. It's fresh, the updated graphics are beautiful keeping a serious tone while also a comedy cartoonish style as the original had. The ghosts are back, and they have been undying to get back into Gravenville! Ghost Master, go and scare!
Return of the Ghost Master is a success. I almost don't remember the original, but the improvements are good and the game is captivating.

Quite a dull game. Idea is neat: by managing a team of ghosts drive out the inhabitants of a some dwelling or achieve some other goal like freeing a spectre bound to a place of his murder. However, execution is not so impressive. First of all, this is a remake of an old game and, while it is said to have some bugs fixed, it is pretty much the same game from what I understand. And that 2000s-era product means hideous visuals, awful audio, redundant menus and horrible UI in general. The ghosts under your command are greenishly bland, the unlucky dwellers you are supposed to scare are copy-pasted models of four kinds, the visual effects and animations are great if we're talking about PlayStation 2. But it would be OK if a game design is OK. Is it OK? Well, not for me. The game itself is somewhat a puzzle: you need to figure out how to achieve your goals by combining powers of the ghosts, but everything seems to be meant to be random. So you're trying the different options with no luck and then surprisingly something happens just because you've occasionally triggered it. Sometimes you seem to understand what you have to do, but doing so gives you nothing, because this is not how the game designers thought it through. Try it only if you have a nostalgia about the original.

​As a kid, I was absolutely obsessed with the original Ghost Master, easily beating it over ten times long before it even made its way to Steam. I vividly remember struggling with those complex, clever puzzles, which makes it all the more painful to see what they’ve done in Resurrection. Aside from the upgraded graphics, this remaster is a total trainwreck of broken mechanics, bugs, and sheer developer laziness that practically plays itself. It honestly makes me want to sit down and cry over what they’ve done to this cult-classic franchise. ​The most embarrassing and infuriating moment for me was seeing how they butchered the mechanics in the first Hospital mission, where you have to get the toy bunny to the child to free a ghost. Good lord, why on earth does the bunny magically teleport itself to the child if no mortal picks it up? What kind of hand-holding babysit-mode is this? Because of casualized garbage like this, the original campaign has become a total breeze that you can blitz through in a measly ten hours max. ​Instead of fixing the quirks of the original, the developers managed to introduce a flood of new issues. While the game is riddled with far more bugs than I can even list, one particular flaw stood out as completely game-breaking. The Mortal Ghostbreakers can now banish your ghosts from across the entire map and through different floors. For instance, I placed Lara (the Vapor ghost) on the first floor of the hospital. Suddenly, with zero warning, some Ghostbreakers walking down the stairs on the third floor triggered a red exclamation mark over my ghost, and I watched them trap her with a comical tractor beam pulling her straight through the ceilings and floors of the entire building. It was exactly because of bugs like this that I wanted to refund the game, but unfortunately, nostalgia got the best of me, I got sucked in, and I passed Steam's two-hour refund window. I’m kicking myself for it. ​To make matters worse, what they did in the DLCs is an absolute crime against the fan base. The original Ghost Master had one thing that was sacred and irreplaceable: a brilliant, iconic Polish dubbing that built the game's dark, satirical atmosphere and beautifully fleshed out the ghosts' backstories. The studio clearly smells of poverty now, because the voiceovers in the add-ons were generated by terrible, soulless AI. It sounds artificial, robotic, and completely dead. Honestly, I have a strong feeling that AI wrote the backstories for these new ghosts, their dialogue, and maybe even the entire concept of Resurrection. The DLC feels like an unwanted acquaintance who shows up to beg you for cash, and instead of saying "thank you," they just spit on your shoes. ​The lack of creativity in these expansions is staggering, relying on peak laziness where mortal characters are shamelessly copy-pasted from previous story missions without even changing their bios. The result is embarrassing; in the drive-in cinema mission, there is a literal duplicate of a character on the map, leaving you with two identical people with the exact same name and biography. Meanwhile, another character gets called into Joe's Diner for interrogation because of the bones found at the old lady's house in a main story mission, which makes absolutely no narrative sense. ​Scaring people in the original was great because we were doing it for a reason, but here, any sense of logic or narrative consistency is completely gone. Why are we constantly stuck in the same tiny town? We have a portal, so why can't the ghosts slowly take over new territories? Right now, I can drive mortals into absolute, gibbering madness, only to return to the map in the next mission to find everything perfectly fine and back to normal. This game won't survive on cheap jump scares and weaponized nostalgia, and it is already actively losing its grip.

As a fan of the original, I was thrilled to dive into *Ghost Master: Resurrection*, and I'm happy to say it doesn't disappoint. This remastered version fixes many of the bugs that made certain missions frustrating in the original, while the enhanced visuals help the game shine on modern hardware. I actually discovered the original *Ghost Master* by chance at a thrift store, complete in its original box. I'll admit, a title like *Ghost Master* made me skeptical at first, but it quickly became one of those hidden gems I couldn't believe I'd overlooked. The gameplay reminds me of *Haunting Starring Polterguy* on the Sega Genesis, while the art style and atmosphere evoke *The Sims: Bustin' Out*. The result is a delightfully spooky world that's equal parts strategy, humor, and nostalgia. As the Ghost Master, your job is to recruit and command a variety of unique ghosts, each with their own supernatural abilities, to complete a series of increasingly creative missions. Success isn't just about causing chaos; you'll need to think strategically, combining different hauntings to frighten specific characters and accomplish multiple objectives. One of my favorite missions has you clearing a sorority house by terrifying its residents, all while working around a coven of Wiccans they've brought in for protection. It's a perfect example of the game's clever mix of puzzle-solving and comedy. Beyond the gameplay, *Ghost Master: Resurrection* is packed with pop culture references, memorable characters, and a tongue-in-cheek sense of humor that gives it plenty of charm. Whether you're revisiting a cult classic or discovering it for the first time, this remaster is an excellent way to experience one of the most original strategy games ever made. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for something fun, quirky, and unlike anything else.
